value.rationale: The motivating paper tests maximum-degree placement as a strong empirical heuristic. Establishing the smallest tree where even its best tie-break is strictly worse gives a sharp, naturally defined structural obstruction, distinct from trivial tied-degree failures. The exhaustive lower-order proof and exact rational gap explain that the effect requires a specific bridge-and-branch topology and are reusable test data for network incentive-placement methods. No unsupported large-network implication is claimed.
